answer: Time-throttled admission resists sybils: the chain admits only a bounded number of new identities per epoch, and each funding source carries a per-window registration cap, so identities can be created only on a slow spiral through time. An operator cannot mint a vault of ten thousand shells in one burst — the flood is stretched across many epochs, giving honeypots and audits a long beacon of time to catch correlated newcomers before any gain standing. Honest growth is organic and fits under the cap; mass-minting is forced into a visible, rate-limited trickle.
